methodology: The study utilized free-radical polymerization to prepare polymers with sulfoxide-protected methacrylate moieties. These were then deprotected via a thermal process and transformed into methacrylate functional groups, which were crosslinked using an oscillatory rheometer in the presence of a radical initiator.
research_objective: To introduce a novel approach to controlling vinyl functionality during polymerization by utilizing sulfoxide chemistry for thermally latent vinyl crosslinking.

key_findings.finding: Thermally latent vinyl crosslinking introduces a novel method for the stepwise and systematic construction of polymeric networks
Sulfoxide chemistry is used to deprotect methacrylate functional groups in polymers, enabling thermal crosslinking reactions.
Thermal-induced radical crosslinking can be controlled by varying the radical concentration or the number of vinyl groups.
The thermal dual-curing approach allows for stepwise and systematic construction of polymer networks, potentially improving final product properties.
Synthesis of SMA-functionalized ethyl acrylate vinyl generating polymer
Preparation of crosslinkable polymer and polymer film
Polymer conversion and thermal stability were investigated.

Choa,*, Seung Man Nohb,*, Hyun-jong Paika,* aDepartment of Polymer Science and Engineering, Pusan National University, Busan 46241, Korea bResearch Center for green fine chemicals, Korea Research Institute of Chemical Technology, Ulsan 44412, Korea cDepartment of Chemistry, Kwangwoon University, Seoul 01897, Korea A R T I C L E I N F O A B S T R A C T Keywords: Radical crosslinking reactions utilizing vinyl functionality are widely used to fabricate polymeric networks for Polymer crosslinking bulk and surface applications. Here, we report a thermally latent vinyl crosslinking of polymers involving Latent crosslinking sulfoxide chemistry for the first time. Polymers with sulfoxide-protected methacrylate moieties are prepared via Vinyl protection free-radical polymerization. These moieties are deprotected by a thermal process and transformed into meth- Sulfoxide chemistry acrylate functional groups. The crosslinking behaviors of the protected polymers are investigated using an oscillatory rheometer in the presence of a radical initiator. The behavior strongly depended on the formation of methacrylate species in polymer chains. The thermally latent crosslinking approach introduces a novel method for the stepwise and systematic construction of polymeric networks that can potentially be applied in dual-curing or patterning processes. 1.
